definitions: A computer security standard introduced to prevent cross-site scripting (XSS), clickjacking, and other code injection attacks resulting from the execution of malicious content in the trusted web page context.

A security mechanism that helps to mitigate certain types of attacks, including Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) and data injection attacks, by specifying which dynamic resources are allowed to load and execute on a web page.
examples: Implementing a robust Content Security Policy is crucial for web application security.
The Content Security Policy blocked the unauthorized script.
Developers often fine-tune their Content Security Policy directives.
